hints.title: Divisibility Constraint
hints.text: For every subarray to have a greatest common divisor of at least F, every single individual element in that subarray must be a multiple of F.

hints.title: Global Factor Invariant
hints.text: Since every element of nums belongs to some subarray in the partition, all elements in nums must be divisible by F.

hints.title: Greatest Common Divisor Reduction
hints.text: The greatest common factor across all elements is simply the cumulative greatest common divisor of the array.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def maximumPartitionFactor(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        # A partition is valid if the array can be partitioned into at most k subarrays
        # such that the common divisor (gcd) of each subarray is at least the candidate factor.
        # Check if a given factor F is feasible:
        # Every element in a subarray must be divisible by F. Thus, EVERY element of nums must be divisible by F!
        # If all elements are divisible by F, the gcd of any subarray is at least F.
        # Therefore, the maximum partition factor is simply the gcd of all elements in nums.
        g = nums[0]
        for x in nums[1:]:
            g = math.gcd(g, x)
        return g
```

complexity.notes: Linear scan with Euclidean greatest common divisor algorithm.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching all partitions leads to exponential combinations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Deduce that the partition constraint forces a global common divisor across all elements.
